options.metric: Annual motorist deaths and annual cyclist deaths
options.denominator: None; annual totals of people killed in police-reported crashes
options.reason: Annual counts show the size and year-to-year movement of fatalities for both groups on a common scale.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths every year, peaking at 139 versus 29 in 2020; in 2025 the counts were 81 versus 23.
options.interpretation: This framing directly compares the annual number of people recorded killed as motorists or cyclists and shows both groups' changes over time. Raw counts are a defensible answer to how many deaths occurred, but they do not adjust for how much each group traveled or otherwise measure individual risk.

options.metric: Annual motorist-death count divided by annual cyclist-death count
options.reason: A yearly ratio makes the relative size of the difference between the two fatality counts easy to compare across years.
options.answer: The motorist-to-cyclist death ratio was highest in 2013 at 10.0:1, lowest in 2019 at 2.65:1, and 3.52:1 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how large the motorist death count was relative to the cyclist death count in each year, with every plotted value above 1 indicating more motorist deaths. It is a defensible scale-free comparison of the two counts, but it does not show their absolute sizes by itself or compare deaths per person or distance traveled.
